caption: The drawing depicts a wooden mechanical device composed of several rectangular and block-shaped elements. The main structure consists of a rectangular base with vertical posts at each end and a horizontal crossbar connecting the tops of the posts. The base and posts are rendered in shades of light and medium brown, suggesting wood grain texture. On the base, two large, block-like forms sit side by side, each with visible angular edges and colored with darker brown and grayish tones. These blocks have rods or levers embedded in them, positioned vertically and diagonally, rendered in brown and metallic gray. Strings or cords, colored in beige or off-white, are attached to the top of the blocks and extend upward, looping over the horizontal crossbar and hanging loosely. Metal brackets and fastenings, depicted in gray with hints of blue, are visible on the front face of the base, securing the blocks in place. To the right of the main figure, there are two smaller schematic pencil drawings, showing simplified front and top outlines of the mechanism, highlighting internal structure and arrangement. The artist's signature, "Henry Waldeck," is written in the lower right corner. The drawing uses a combination of watercolor and pencil, with the main object in color and the schematic views in pencil on a plain, light-colored background.
title: Rat Trap
